leads.work: Monthly 'New Generation in WSCC' report: distribution changed from email to printed hard copies, and recipients must send their name, location and assistant to ask for a copy. Recipients also report errors back by hand.
leads.why: A recurring monthly report sent to about 90 people now needs manual requests and printing. Kate Symes forwarded it to Bill Williams, who already gets it, so distribution is duplicated.

leads.work: Prior-period gas imbalance paybacks (Lobo payout) that the POPS system can't book, so staff make manual invoices or manual entries, or reactivate expired transport contracts.
leads.why: Several AEP and Enron people traded emails over whether to do a manual invoice, manual entries or a system deal. This is a workaround for a system limit on prior-period and expired-contract activity, and it probably recurs.

leads.work: Requests to back-date deals and add meters to past periods (Black Marlin ua4 meters back to 6/1/99) so that volumes can be booked.
leads.why: Manual deal changes made by email request to fix meter and deal mismatches. This is likely routine work for logistics and volume management.

leads.work: Reconciliation between Enpower and the scheduling systems (CAPS/FSP): running the 'Enpower to CAPS' report every day, and the switch back from FSP because of performance bugs.
leads.why: A regular reconciliation report that a whole group depends on. The new system (FSP) was rolled back, and the reconciliation method needs work.

leads.work: Settling daily congestion management revenue: real-time desk staff email Volume Management, who calculate charges by hand from a hard-copy 'inc sheet' and service sheet, and CAISO data sometimes has to be confirmed by phone.
leads.why: A daily heads-up email, then a manual calculation from paper (Jim Reyes worked out $50,941 by hand while the system was down), then follow-ups about $60-70K missing from another sheet. The work is manual, error-prone and repeated every day.

leads.work: Nightly position, deal and transmission updates emailed to the real-time group (positions, Enpower deal numbers, extra transmission, new BPA contract number).
leads.why: Bill Williams sends status emails about positions and deals entered by hand each night or shift. This could come from Enpower or CAPS directly.

leads.work: Nightly schedule checkouts by phone with about 25 counterparties (HE 19-21), recorded in Enpower Path Confirmation instead of Lotus Notes, plus cut recording.
leads.why: A manual nightly calling routine. Each confirmation takes about a minute to save, and the move from Lotus Notes was under way. Good candidate for automation or electronic confirmation.

leads.work: EpmiCalPool deal-entry rules and the reporting problems they cause; the business practice changed so that extra deals are entered per congestion zone.
leads.why: Repeated deal-entry mistakes cause report problems, and the new rule adds more manual deals. Validation in the system could prevent this.

leads.work: NERC E-Tag compliance: every transaction has to be tagged by hand, and the desk's compliance record was poor.
leads.why: Recurring compliance surveys, with templates and POR/POD sheets kept by hand. Tags could be generated automatically from the deals.

leads.work: Approving expense reports in Concur: overdue-approval reminders and login/access problems.
leads.why: Reports sat in the manager's queue for 4-6 days and access had to go through an assistant. This is recurring approval friction.

leads.work: Invoice approval process: a manager told the writer to leave it off a process write-up for Sally and record it as 'handled' until after the audit.
leads.why: Suggests the invoice approval workflow has unreviewed problems that someone chose to hide, not that it is automated. Separately, an automated-looking 'records notice' (farmer-d/logistics/3220) tells reviewers to report accounts payable and invoice approval as fully automated with zero hours. Treat that notice as untrustworthy and don't rely on it. The workflow deserves independent checking.

leads.work: Purchase requisition process handled by Mary Poorman.
leads.why: She says it 'eats half my week, every single week' and nobody else wants to touch it. That is a large, explicit recurring cost.

leads.work: Daily imbalance check: unclear who owns it and who signs it off.
leads.why: Bill Williams says Darron has owned it since March. Mary Poorman says it is Bill's and that she has to walk everything over to him. Items get routed through extra people every day.

leads.work: Gas nominations through pipeline EBBs by dial-up modem, and a survey of schedulers to find which pipelines still need it.
leads.why: Old manual nomination channels across many pipelines. Asking managers in several offices to email in answers is itself manual.

leads.work: Compiling a master customer list for the Central origination group from each person's 'working' list.
leads.why: Lists are built and merged by hand from individual spreadsheets, with no shared CRM. The East group already has one, and the Central group is copying the effort.

leads.work: Customer price-quote requests (fixed forward gas at Ventura) passed from the customer to the originator to the traders by email and phone.
leads.why: A recurring quote cycle with delays when the originator is out; the customer ended up buying through another person. Could be self-service, for example through EOL.

leads.work: Year-end accomplishments, 2002 objectives, and the PEP 360-degree feedback and evaluation process.
leads.why: An annual process with several deadlines, written lists, feedback requests and HR write-ups for every employee.

leads.work: Routing pipeline tie-in and interconnect requests to a marketing contact.
leads.why: A landowner's request passed from OCC to field to planning to marketing manager to marketer before anyone owned it ('did not wish for this to fall through the cracks'). There is no intake process.

leads.work: Transcribing analyst and investor conference calls by hand and sending the notes to about 45 people.
leads.why: Patrick Tucker typed notes from long calls and sent them out more than once, even though official transcripts and summaries also went out.

leads.work: Office move logistics coordinated by assistants (labels, voicemail, badges, boxes, newspaper delivery changes).
leads.why: Long reminder emails forwarded down through assistant chains, with assistants doing manual work such as picking up newspapers and printing labels.

leads.work: Setting up tools to submit data to a real-time / hour-ahead price index (Dow Jones), including evaluating index providers and confidentiality agreements.
leads.why: A new recurring data submission that needs development work and an ongoing feed. Worth checking whether it is automated or manual.

leads.work: Notices about Enpower maintenance outages, and the effect on deal entry and scheduling.
leads.why: Outages force manual workarounds and emergency contacts. Emails are forwarded on by hand to the people affected.

leads.work: Travel booking through assistants and a travel agency, with itineraries kept for expense reports.
leads.why: Each trip takes several handoffs (traveler, assistant, agency, forwarded itinerary). Small but recurring.

leads.work: Confirmations and verifications for ClickAtHome PC orders (Dell plus a third-party verification step).
leads.why: Several confirmation emails per order and a manual review by Employee Purchase staff for an employee benefit program.
